description: Task 2.5 - Go runtime hook. The Go binding (xplainit-go/xplainit.go) is a CGO wrapper over the C FFI exposing New/Enable/Disable/GetEvents/ClearEvents/GetStatistics but no way to record function events from Go code. Add a Go-facing tracing API and prove a real Go program captures events end to end. Toolchains go 1.25.1 and gcc are PRESENT and the C library (libxplainit_c) builds, so CGO linking is feasible in-sandbox. This task DEPENDS ON FEAT-004 (it reuses the new C FFI recording entry points xplainit_on_function_enter/exit/exception). Files: xplainit-go/xplainit.go, xplainit-go/examples/basic.go, new xplainit-go/xplainit_test.go, xplainit-go/README.md.
steps: Add Go methods that wrap the new C FFI recording functions from FEAT-004: (x *Xplainit) OnFunctionEnter(name, file string, line int), OnFunctionExit(name, file string, line int), OnException(errType, message, file string, line int). Use C.CString with defer C.free for each string argument, following the existing CGO idioms in xplainit.go. Update the cgo preamble #include if needed (header path already points at ../xplainit-c/include).

Provide a convenient Go tracing helper following the plan's 'function wrapping' option: e.g. a `Trace(name string) func()` that records enter immediately and returns a closure to be `defer`-ed which records exit - the idiomatic Go pattern (`defer x.Trace("myfunc")()`). This is the realistic Go instrumentation approach (no automatic sys.settrace equivalent); document that automatic instrumentation would require delve or codegen (out of scope) and that this manual/defer wrapper is the supported mechanism.

Expand xplainit-go/examples/basic.go to use New/Enable, trace a simple function, a recursive function, and an error path via the defer-Trace helper and OnException, then print GetEvents/GetStatistics. It must build with CGO against target/release/libxplainit_c.

Add xplainit-go/xplainit_test.go with `go test` cases that create a tracer, record enter/exit/exception, and assert GetStatistics/GetEvents reflect the recorded events (parse the JSON). Ensure the test sets the needed cgo LDFLAGS/rpath or runs with CGO_LDFLAGS/LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing at target/release so the C lib resolves.

Build and run: `cargo build --release` (to produce libxplainit_c), then from xplainit-go run `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` (with LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../target/release or equivalent), and run the example. Confirm real events are captured.

Update xplainit-go/README.md with the honest status: manual/defer-based tracing works and is verified; automatic instrumentation (delve/codegen) is future work. If CGO linking genuinely cannot resolve the C lib in-sandbox, capture the exact error and document the required LD_LIBRARY_PATH/rpath rather than faking success.
acceptance_criteria: xplainit-go/xplainit.go exposes OnFunctionEnter/OnFunctionExit/OnException and a defer-friendly Trace helper that record events through the C FFI.
`go test ./...` in xplainit-go passes and asserts recorded events appear in GetEvents/GetStatistics.
The example builds with CGO and, when run, prints non-empty captured events including expected function names.
cargo build --release, cargo test, cargo clippy -D warnings all pass; Python suites remain green.
README states the honest status (manual/defer tracing verified; automatic instrumentation future work).
verification: cd xplainit-go && LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../target/release CGO_LDFLAGS='-L../target/release -lxplainit_c' go test ./...
findings:
Implemented and verified end to end. Added OnFunctionEnter/OnFunctionExit/OnException (each C.CString + defer C.free, line as C.uint32_t) and a defer-friendly Trace(name,file,line) func() helper to xplainit-go/xplainit.go. Removed a pre-existing unused `encoding/json` import from xplainit.go (the package would not compile with it, so the module had never been built cleanly before). Expanded examples/basic.go (simple, recursive factorial, error path via OnException) and added xplainit_test.go (7 tests, stdlib encoding/json only). Updated README.md with honest status: manual/defer tracing verified, automatic instrumentation (delve/codegen) is future work, plus exact build/run commands.

Verification (all green): `cargo build --release` clean; `cargo test --release` all pass; `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean (no Rust changed). From xplainit-go: `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../target/release CGO_LDFLAGS='-L../target/release -lxplainit_c' go test ./...` => ok (7/7). `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=../target/release go run ./examples/basic.go` captured real events including simpleGreeting enter/exit, nested factorial recursion enter/exit, and a DivisionByZero Exception. gofmt clean, go vet clean. Did not touch xplainit-python.

KEY FINDINGS for downstream work:
1. A freshly created C handle is ENABLED BY DEFAULT (xplainit_create sets enabled=true); no Enable() call is required to record, and the disabled-path test must call Disable() first.
2. The C FFI xplainit_get_statistics counts ONLY the dedicated error enum variants (DivisionByZero/NullPointerError/IndexOutOfBounds) as `errors`. A generic Exception event (what OnException records) is captured and visible in GetEvents but is NOT tallied into the Errors statistic (stays 0). Tests assert the exception via the events JSON, not the stats counter.
3. Confirmed the drain behavior: both GetEvents and GetStatistics drain the store; example and tests account for this by reading stats first then re-recording before reading events.
4. Event JSON is externally-tagged serde: array of {"FunctionEnter":{...}}, {"FunctionExit":{...}}, {"Exception":{error_type,message,...}}.
